page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.large is a compute-oriented virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. The CPU incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA extensions. The instance is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is not bundled, necessitating attached cloud storage, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reflect predictable performance bounded by the small dual-thread physical allocation. In single-core compute operations, such as stress-ng single-core (1858.29) and Geekbench single-core (1559.0), the instance achieves median-tier results. Single-threaded gzip compression performs solidly at 27.69 GB/sec. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded capacity remains low across synthetic suites due to the single physical core architecture, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 1813.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2990.49. Large-block memory transfers achieve 14.89 GB/sec read and 13.52 GB/sec write bandwidth, while static web serving throughput reaches 3.56 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the server provides dedicated CPU resources without the uncertainty of burstable credit models, although its low memory footprint limits concurrency. Without bundled NVMe storage or GPU acceleration, this configuration is best suited for lightweight web servers, reverse proxies, small microservices, and continuous integration or development tasks with modest resource requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.9 GHz, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs sourced from a single physical core with hyperthreading, alongside 4 GB of system memory. The processor includes hardware acceleration for AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic operations. The instance lacks bundled local storage, requiring external block volumes, and includes a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark testing indicates mid-tier single-threaded CPU capability, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1559.0 and steady compression speeds, while multi-core operations reflect the constraints of its two-thread limit. Memory write throughput measures 13.52 GB/sec for large blocks. Without GPU hardware, this configuration provides cost-conscious compute density suitable for lightweight web serving, small-scale microservices, routine background scripts, and dev-test environments requiring predictable dedicated CPU threads.
